ARABIC — TERMLY EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Only memorise without using the language
   C. Avoid speaking to classmates
   D. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

2. When practising Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.

3. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.

4. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.

5. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

6. When practising Conversational Skills: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills: Etiquette.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills: Etiquette.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills: Etiquette.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills: Etiquette.

7. When practising Conversational Skills: Interviews, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills: Interviews.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills: Interviews.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills: Interviews.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills: Interviews.

8. When practising Public Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Public Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Public Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Public Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Public Speaking.

9. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

10. When practising Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.

11. When practising Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension and Critical Reading Skills.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Study Skills: The Reading Process and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Mechanics of Writing: The Arabic Calligraphy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Social Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Functional Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Creative Writing: Poems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
